newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian light sweet crude grades firm, Oman troubled.
newsitem.headline: Asian light sweet crude grades firm, Oman troubled.

text.p: Light sweet crude oils in Asia were underpinned on Wednesday on middle distillate demand while troubled Oman showed signs of further pressure.

November Brent/Dubai paper was $2.12/$2.25 per barrel. December and February Brent/Dubai traded late Tuesday at $1.98 and $1.70 respectively, with a Wall Street trader taking a December/February Brent/Dubai spread of 28 cents.
The Dubai intermonth market was steady, with near months around 41 cents backwardation.
In the wet market, light sweet crudes were talked higher on demand for middle distillate rich crudes.
A producer was offering Tapis at a premium of $1.00 compared with a last trade done a week ago at 95 cents.

Cossack, which traded earlier this week at APPI Tapis quotes less 20 cents, was offered at flat to quotes, while Kutubu, which last traded at a discount of 30 cents under Tapis was being offered by a major at a premium of 10 to 15 cents.
Paper Tapis rose strongly to be quoted late Wednesday at $23.15/$23/35 for October versus a day-earlier $22.45/$22.60.
Traders said the price was catching up with the firm NYMEX futures price which it had lagged for some days.
Amid further indications of a firmer light sweet market, November Murban traded twice at a premium of 25 cents. Last deals done were around 20 cents.

The first November Oman traded at November Dubai quotes plus 84 cents between two majors. Traders said the trade reflected a weak view of the Oman official price, which retroactively for August stood at 96 cents above Dubai.

October overhang barrels were said to be offered as low as 25 cents below MPM with a bid 40 cents below that to factor in month-on-month backwardation. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, Miho Yoshikawa, (+813 5473 3706)
